newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-FANS RIOT AT BASTIA, MARSEILLE, PSG FORGE AHEAD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FANS RIOT AT BASTIA, MARSEILLE, PSG FORGE AHEAD.

text.p: Angry Bastia fans hurled missiles on to the pitch after an unpunished tackle by Monaco's Emmanuel Petit left Slovakian striker Lubomir Moravcik with a fractured ankle in a 0-0 draw in the French first division on Saturday.

And fans in Marseille, angry at their team's shock 1-0 home defeat by a Caen side that had not won before this season, hurled stones at police and had to be dispersed by tear gas. Several policemen were slightly hurt.

The Bastia fans at the Furiani stadium, scene of riots that left 15 people dead during an ill-fated French Cup match against Marseille five years ago, reacted when Petit also went in hard on Moravcik's substitute in the second half.
Play was held up for several minutes and a missile struck the referee on the head. But when the fans had calmed down the match resumed.
Outside's Marseille's Velodrome ground, scene of euphoria in the glory days of the former European champions, several players needed police protection from angry fans as they left after the match.

A police officer said: "These incidents, rare in Marseille, were caused but only a few dozen people and were only due to their disappointment at seeing OM (Olympique Marseille) beaten on their own ground."
The draw at Bastia left both sides joint third as champions Auxerre climbed above them with a 1-0 home win over Lens.

Midfielder Antoine Sibierski, likely also to stand in for injured captain Sabri Lamouchi in the crucial European Cup champions' league clash with Grasshopper Zurich on Wednesday, converted a penalty in the 76th minute.
Brazilian midfielder Leonardo scored his seventh goal of the season as Paris Saint-Germain won 1-0 at Metz to go seven points clear at the top.
Leonardo struck in the 32nd minute following a rebound from a shot by fellow Brazilian Rai.
Bottom club Nancy, like penultimate Caen, also won for the first time -- and away, too. They beat Jean-Pierre Papin's Bordeaux with an early goal by Northern Ireland forward Phil Gray.
Bordeaux, beaten at home for the second time in a row, had forward Kaba Diawara sent off in the dying minutes for dissent after the referee declined to give Papin what looked like a valid penalty.
Three other players were sent off, taking the season's total to 28 in 12 rounds of matches.

Guingamp's French international defender Vicent Candela, capped for the first time in midweek, was shown the red card near the end of his team's 2-1 loss at in-form Strasbourg, who climbed six places to fifth.
Striker David Zitelli's third-minute opening goal for Strssbourg was his third in two games and took him to the top of the scorers list with nine.
Nantes, who routed Nice 7-0 in their first victory of the season last weekend, were lucky to come away from Lille with a point after a late equaliser gave them a 3-3 draw.

Japhet N'Doram put Nantes in front with a penalty, but a penalty at the other end by Miladin Becanovic after halk an hour ended teenager Mickael Landreau's two-match run of clean sheets in the Nantes goal.
Becanovic put the home side ahead before the interval, Jocelyn Gourvennec equalised and Franck Renou, on loan from Nantes, put Lille in front again before Decroix's decisive 88th-minute strike.
Defender Teddy Bertin converted two penalties in Le Havre's 4-1 home win over Lyon, who played the better football but were guilty of poor finishing.
